evidence.note: Token endpoint rejected the code exchange
Matches the reported AADSTS501481 PKCE failure
The challenge must be BASE64URL(SHA256(code_verifier)) of the exact verifier sent on the token request

output.fix: Make sure the code_verifier sent to the token endpoint is the exact one that produced the code_challenge in the authorization request. Generate one verifier for each authorization attempt, and store it per-session or per-state. Don't regenerate it on redirect, on a second tab, or on a retry. Compute the challenge as BASE64URL-without-padding(SHA256(verifier)) with method S256. Confirm the verifier isn't truncated, re-encoded, or altered in storage or transport. It must be 43–128 unreserved characters. Then restart the flow to get a fresh authorization code.

alternatives.why_not: invalid_grant can also mean an expired or reused code, but the description names the code verifier specifically.
Client type, redirect URI, and method are consistent with the configuration, and the error points at the verifier.

questions: Is the code_verifier sent in the token request the same value that was used to derive the code_challenge in this authorization request, or could it come from a different session or tab?
